items.title: Devices used to nab dangerous drivers in Dubai might be a fit for Mississauga: city
items.summary: Mississauga is looking to technology being used on the other side of the world in an effort to clamp down on noisy cars that dangerously race along city streets. While Peel Regional Police regularly target illegal street racing — and cars with modified/excessively loud exhaust systems — through both routine patrols and specific enforcement campaigns, Mayor Carolyn Parrish said on Wednesday the City of Mississauga might be able to beef up its own enforcement when it comes to the illegal road activity. “We get these guys with the (noisy) mufflers and the nonsense, and there are certain streets (in Mississauga) that are freeways, and they are racetracks…,” Parrish said at the city’s general committee meeting, adding that perhaps a high-tech enforcement tool already being used in Dubai, in the United Arab Emirates, to nab noisy and dangerous street racers might be of use in Mississauga. She said there appears to be “a big problem” with noisy street racers in Dubai, where authorities are now using devices that record the loud vehicles and capture their licence plates. In Dubai, where police say reckless vehicle modifications and excessive noise are on many occasions linked to dangerous driving, authorities are using AI-enabled noise-detection radar to catch vehicles that exceed legal sound limits, according to Wired Middle East. The high-tech devices, which are mounted on roadside poles, measure noise intensity, identify the source (cars) of the sound and automatically record violations, a report earlier this year from Wired noted. Georgios Fthenos, the City of Mississauga’s director of enforcement, says staff are familiar with the technology being used in Dubai.

items.title: WEIGHELL: David “Keith” of Exeter, formerly of Mississauga
items.summary: SEPTEMBER 24, 2026 BY HASKETT FUNERAL HOME LEAVE A CONDOLENCE Passed away at home on Tuesday, September 22, 2026 at the age of 83. Adored grandpa of Keith and Zach, Stefanie and Jake; Kayla and Thomas, and Tyler and Lindsay. Dear brother-in-law of Gail Weighell and Gord and Joan Denley. items.title: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants the TTC subway extended to Mississauga’s city centre. But will Doug Ford buy in?
items.summary: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants to extend Toronto’s Line 2 subway to Mississauga’s city centre. Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is proposing to extend the TTC’s Line 2 subway from Kipling to Mississauga city centre, creating a central transit hub. Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie says it’s time for an extension of the east-west Bloor-Danforth subway line to Mississauga’s city centre — and if elected she will launch a feasibility study and appeal to a subway-loving premier and a prime minister looking for nation-building projects. “Vaughan has a subway and one is being planned for both Markham and Richmond Hill. ” said Crombie in an interview. ” The Hurontario LRT or Hazel McCallion line, which is currently under construction as a north-south spine that will extend through Mississauga’s city centre into Brampton, made sense at the time of planning more than a decade ago and was the more affordable option, Crombie said. “We didn’t have the density then, but we do have the density today and we have the demand for it,” she said. Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election as mayor, has been a fan of the idea of a Mississauga subway for several years, and lamented that McCallion shot the idea down when she was mayor decades ago. But Parrish has also cited the hefty price tag as a barrier, unless the province is willing to pick up the tab of $1 billion per kilometre. “Listen, if somebody is going to put a subway out to Mississauga, there’s no way anybody in their right mind would turn it down with traffic (as it is) now,” Parrish told Insauga last year. Parrish did not respond to a request for comment Thursday.

items.summary: Extending the Toronto subway line to Square One in Mississauga has been discussed countless times over the past several decades — and the notion is being raised again by one of the high-profile candidates running for mayor of Canada’s seventh-largest city. ” Crombie, who served as Mississauga mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, added it’s time to deliver a subway to the City Centre area. “Mississauga is one of Canada’s largest cities. items.title: Peel Police Boost Patrols Near Malton Money Lender After Shots Fired, but Say No Wider Threat
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, officers are investigating after shots were fired at a money lending business near the Mississauga-Brampton border, in the Malton area near Morning Star Drive and Jolliffe Avenue. Police say the shooting happened Thursday and that no injuries were reported. Investigators say residents in the area can expect to see a heavier police presence as the investigation continues. Despite the shooting, police say there is no broader threat to public safety. Anyone with information about the incident is asked to contact Peel Regional Police, and tips can also be submitted anonymously through Crime Stoppers, which police say can pay out a reward of up to $2,000 for information that leads to an arrest.

items.title: Parrish and Crombie Set for Their First Face-Off of the Campaign at a Business-Focused Debate
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's highest-profile mayoral candidates will share a debate stage for the first time this election season on Friday afternoon, in an event hosted by the Mississauga Board of Trade. The 2026 Mississauga Mayoral Debate, scheduled for September 25, will focus on issues important to the city's business community, including economic growth, leadership, investment, infrastructure and the city's future, according to organizers. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie are both expected to take part, laying out their plans on business issues, fielding questions from a moderator and engaging directly with each other. Organizers say the debate is meant to give business leaders, entrepreneurs, professionals and other engaged residents a chance to hear directly from the candidates about their vision for the city. The event comes as the campaign heads toward the October 26 municipal election, with more debates expected in the weeks ahead.

items.title: Ward 1's Longtime Councillor Faces a Single Challenger in Mississauga's October Election
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, two candidates are running to represent Mississauga's Ward 1 at City Hall in the October 26 municipal election, with one incumbent councillor facing a single new challenger. The incumbent, first elected as Ward 1's city and regional councillor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022, told the paper they currently chair the city's Road Safety Committee and serve as vice-chair of both the Budget Committee and the Environmental Action Committee. The councillor said their priority is to keep delivering practical leadership for Ward 1 while pushing for the ward to receive its fair share of investment in infrastructure, transportation, parks, public safety and community services. Public safety and road safety remain central priorities, according to the councillor, who pointed to effective policing, community-based programs and traffic-calming measures as ways to make neighbourhoods safer. The incumbent also said future growth needs to follow the city's official plan, respect existing neighbourhoods and come with the infrastructure, parks and community amenities residents need. Mississauga.com is running similar candidate profiles for wards across the city ahead of the election.

items.title: Crombie proposes subway extension into Mississauga in election bid
items.summary: Mississauga mayoral hopeful Bonnie Crombie is pitching the idea of extending Toronto’s subway network into her city, hoping that, if she wins, she can convince Premier Doug Ford to fund the plan. Unveiling her transit proposals on Thursday, Crombie said she wanted to see Line 2 extended westward from Kipling Station into downtown Mississauga, with a stop at Square One via Sherway Gardens. “For the first time, residents should ultimately be able to board the subway in Mississauga and ride directly into Toronto,” Crombie wrote. “Toronto has already directed planning work on a possible Line 2 extension from Kipling to Sherway Gardens. ” Crombie served as Mississauga mayor from 2014 to 2024, leaving the post to become leader of the Ontario Liberal Party. She is running against incumbent Carolyn Parrish, as well as councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla and several other candidates to take control of city council. Tedjo’s campaign said a subway extension may be a “dream worth pursuing” but stressed a better relationship “with the province to secure the support and funding needed to make it happen” must be the first step. Damela said the key was delivering “realistic” transit.

items.title: Crombie Pitches a Kipling-to-Square-One Subway Extension as the Centerpiece of Her Mayoral Platform
items.summary: According to CityNews, Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie unveiled a transportation plan on Thursday centered on extending Toronto's TTC Line 2 subway west from Kipling Station through Sherway Gardens into downtown Mississauga, creating a direct subway link between the two cities for the first time. Crombie said Mississauga residents are spending too much of their lives stuck in traffic, and CityNews reports she would spend her first year in office pursuing a formal partnership with the province, Metrolinx, the TTC and the City of Toronto to study the extension's routes, station locations, ridership projections and costs. Crombie suggested exploring whether part of the route could run above ground along the Dundas corridor to help control costs, according to CityNews. The Star reports that Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election, has also long favoured a Mississauga subway but has pointed to its roughly one billion dollar per kilometre price tag as a major obstacle unless the province agrees to cover it. According to Global News, Crombie, who served as Mississauga's mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, is running against Parrish along with councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, among other candidates. Global News reports that Tedjo's campaign called the subway idea a dream worth pursuing but said securing provincial funding and support has to come first, while Damerla said the priority should be delivering realistic transit improvements.
